title: Hybrid rendering strategy and gesture resilience for tables, charts, and modals in Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a resilient Console surface that combines canvas-svg hybrid rendering with cross-browser gesture and scroll smoothing. Scope includes primary dashboard tables, interactive charts (canvas-based), and modal stacking behavior on touch devices and high-DPI zoom states. Reduce rendering-related layout shifts, eliminate tooltip clipping on iOS Safari, and provide a graceful SVG fallback for environments where WebGL/canvas accelerations cause artifacts.

Why this matters: Customers rely on Console for fast triage (alerts, rollouts, cost analytics). Visual hiccups on certain browsers increase cognitive load for SREs and PMs during incidents. This work prevents churn and reduces support tickets tied to rendering/interaction regressions.

Success criteria:
- No critical rendering glitches (overlapping tooltips, clipped axes, unscrollable modal content) across Chrome, Safari (macOS + iOS), Firefox, and Edge in supported breakpoints.
- Canvas charts have an SVG fallback that matches key visual states and keeps interactive annotations accessible to AT (assistive tech).
- Table virtualization preserves keyboard focus and selection when density collapses at small breakpoints.
- Modal stacking: background inertness enforced, body scroll locked with smooth restoration on close, and focus return deterministic.

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype demonstrating dense/table collapse, chart-to-SVG fallback toggle, and stacked modal flows (desktop + small-screen).
- Engineering acceptance checklist and a small test harness (Cypress + visual snapshot cases).
- Design spec with browser-specific mitigation notes (e.g., -webkit-overflow-scrolling, pointer-event workarounds for iOS tooltips).

Design trade-offs considered:
- Full SVG charts would simplify accessibility but increase bundle size and reduce performance for very large series. We chose hybrid canvas primary + SVG fallback for limited states (hover/annotate/export) to balance cost and accessibility.
- Aggressive virtualization reduces DOM size but complicates keyboard navigation; to mitigate, we persist a lightweight focus-anchor element outside virtualized window.

Open questions for review:
- Acceptable visual parity threshold between canvas and SVG fallback (pixel-perfect vs. semantic parity).
- Toggle surface for QA to force SVG fallback in prod for debugging.

Accessibility notes:
- All interactive annotations must expose aria-label or aria-describedby.
- Ensure focus trapping for modals and deterministic focus return.
- Provide a reduced-motion variant for chart animations per user preferences.
comments: 2026-02-12 — Kickoff: alignment meeting with Eng (Jae Kim), PM (Lena Ortiz), and Research (Ben Cho). Agreed hybrid approach and scoped to three dashboards: Rollouts, Cost, and Inference Latency.
2026-02-20 — Prototype v1 uploaded to Figma. Early feedback: Safari iOS clipping still visible; requested a dedicated note for -webkit-overflow-scrolling fixes.
2026-02-26 — Eng spike completed (ENG-5032). Confirmed that canvas artifacts on Firefox are reproducible at 125% zoom; workaround uses devicePixelRatio-aware redraw throttling.
2026-03-02 — Design pass: added keyboard focus-anchor pattern for virtualized tables. PM asked for a compact-density toggle in header to enable user-driven collapse.
2026-03-06 — Accessibility review with Research: annotations should provide text alternatives; motion reduced flag implemented in prototype. Minor wording changes to aria labels suggested.

2026-03-09 — QA notes: Cypress snapshots created for Chrome, macOS Safari, iOS Safari (simulator), and Firefox. Two visual diffs remain outstanding (tooltip overlap on iOS and axis aliasing in Firefox at 125% zoom).
2026-03-10 — Current: PRs open: GH-Redwood/console#7842 (canvas-to-svg fallback helper) and GH-Redwood/console#7846 (modal-body-scroll-lock). Awaiting Eng review and perf signoff.
